THE TEXTURE MODEL, verified today from primary source rather than assumed. GenerateCubemap(stage3, kNoise) writes six 64x64 slices in face order +X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z, each from GenerateSwizzledRGBMaxContrastNoisePattern with a per-face seed from {0x0000FF, 0xFF00FF, 0x00FF00, 0x00FFFF, 0xFF0000, 0xFFFF00}. The generator XORs that seed, it does not mask: r = (x%2)*255, g = (y%2)*255, b = ((x/2+y/2)%2)*255, then each XORed with the seed byte. So EVERY face carries all eight colour-cube corners at 1-2 texel granularity -- R in one-pixel vertical stripes, G in one-pixel horizontal stripes, B in a 2x2 checker -- seed-permuted per face. The issue's phrase 'the eight corners of the colour cube' is CORRECT. I record that because I first read kColorMasks as a mask, concluded the faces were six single hues, and was about to publish that the issue's premise was wrong. Reading the generator refuted me. THE NEW CONSTRAINT: silicon reaches ONLY ODD-PARITY CORNERS. Over all six goldens, 348,622 quad pixels, every colour produced is a corner with an odd number of channels at 255 -- #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF, #FFFFFF. Not one pixel is black, magenta, cyan or yellow, the four even-parity corners. So the three selected bits satisfy r^g^b = 1: THE THIRD COMPONENT IS DETERMINED BY THE OTHER TWO. That is the same statement the sign table implies -- solving the table for the three channel bits gives one channel as the XOR of the other two -- so two independent measurements agree: the doc's per-pixel sign correlation, and the goldens' colour set, which never saw a sign. ONE MORE OBSERVATION, not yet a constraint: silicon produces flat regions of 13,000 to 29,000 pixels of a single corner from a texture that alternates corners every one or two texels, so its coordinate is constant over large screen areas. It saturates; it does not sample a varying coordinate.
